page: Amazon Web Services c6id.large is a compute-optimized instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 2 vCPUs allocated from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 118 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities but limited multi-core scaling. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the average category, supported by hardware features like AVX-512 and AES cryptography instructions. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, register in the lower percentiles due to the dual-vCPU constraint. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both read and write operations are also positioned in the lower tier, with large-block uncached reads measuring 14.19 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the c6id.large offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring dedicated compute resources and fast local NVMe storage without requiring massive memory allocations. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage provides low-latency disk access, though the 4.0 GB memory capacity presents a clear tradeoff for memory-intensive applications.

This instance is best suited for single-threaded or light multi-threaded compute tasks, basic web serving, lightweight cryptography, and development environments that benefit from fast local scratch space.
